exercises.heading: 11.1. Exercises

list.item: What is a sequence?
What does it mean to say that $$\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}a_{n} = 8$$ ?
What does it mean to say that $$\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}a_{n} = \infty$$ ?

solution.paragraph: A sequence is an ordered list of numbers. It can also be defined as a function whose domain is the set of positive integers.
The terms $$a_{n}$$ approach $$8$$ as $$n$$ becomes large.
The terms $$a_{n}$$ become large as $$n$$ becomes large.

list.item: What is a convergent sequence? Give two examples.
What is a divergent sequence? Give two examples.

problem.paragraph: Suppose you know that $$\left\{ a_{n} \right\}$$ is a decreasing sequence and all its terms lie between the numbers $$5$$ and $$8$$ . Explain why the sequence has a limit. What can you say about the value of the limit?

solution.paragraph: Convergent by the Monotonic Sequence Theorem; $$5 \leqslant L < 8$$

list.item: Fibonacci posed the following problem: Suppose that rabbits live forever and that every month each pair produces a new pair which becomes productive at age $$2$$ months. If we start with one newborn pair, how many pairs of rabbits will we have in the $$n$$ th month? Show that the answer is $$f_{n}$$ , where $$\left\{ f_{n} \right\}$$ is the Fibonacci sequence defined in Example 3(c).
Let $$a_{n} = f_{n + 1} \slash f_{n}$$ and show that $$a_{n - 1} = 1 + 1 \slash a_{n - 2}$$ . Assuming that $$\left\{ a_{n} \right\}$$ is convergent, find its limit.

Let $$a_{1} = a$$ , $$a_{2} = f(a)$$ , $${a_{3} = f\left( a_{2} \right) = f\left( {f(a)} \right)},\ldots,{a_{n + 1} = f\left( a_{n} \right)}$$ , where $$f$$ is a continuous function. If $$\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}a_{n} = L$$ , show that $$f(L) = L$$ .
Illustrate part (a) by taking $$f(x) = \cos x$$ , $$a = 1$$ , and estimating the value of $$L$$ to five decimal places.

Use a graph to guess the value of the limit $$\lim\limits_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{n^{5}}{n!}$$ Details Three curves and a line are graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The first curve, labeled y = sin(x), is a sinusoidal curve, that enters from the left and immediately goes down to the right, crosses the negative x-axis, reaches a low point, goes up to the right, crosses the origin, reaches a high point, goes down to the right, crosses the x-axis, completing a full wave and exits at the right. The line, labeled T_1, enters from the bottom, slopes upward to the right, runs along the curve y as it goes up to the right, crossing the origin, and exits at the top. The second curve, labeled T_3, is a wave-like curve, that enters from the top, goes down to the right, crosses the negative x-axis, reaches a low point, goes up to the right, and runs along y and T_1 as they pass through the origin and ascend in the first quadrant, veers away from them and reaches a high point, goes down to the right, crosses the positive x-axis, and exits at the bottom. The thor curve, labeled T_5, is a wave-like curve, that enters from the bottom, briefly goes up to the right, concave down, reaches a high point in the third quadrant, goes down to the right, and runs along y as it reaches a low point, rises, crosses the origin and rises an reaches a high point in the first quadrant, veers away and briefly goes down to the right, reaches a low point in the first quadrant, goes up to the right and exits at the top.
